sn.c: The Dress Circle overhang starts at row Q but mainly blocks the top of the stage in the last Orchestra rows, W to ZZ.
sn.sh: Overhang blocks the top of the stage in the last rows

sn.c: At either end of Balcony row A, seats 25 to 30 curve round to the side, and the angle and wall block the stage when seated.
sn.sh: Row A end seats curve away from the stage

sn.c: In the Left Balcony, the safety bar can be too high for shorter people and distracting in the front rows.
sn.sh: High safety bar in the front rows

sn.c: The back rows of the Center Balcony give a fair view at a very good price, with better than average legroom.
sn.sh: Fair views at a very good price

sn.c: Legroom is generous across the whole Orchestra, so you do not need an aisle seat to stretch out.
Two private Boxes sit raised beside the Left Balcony, with fairly good views of the stage.

vs.sum: One of Broadway's largest houses (1,930 seats across four levels), the Lyric's sheer scale means rear orchestra and mezzanine seats sit far from the stage, with sightline obstructions from balcony overhangs. Acoustics are solid and the theater's modern construction makes it well-suited for spectacle productions.

acc.note: 42nd St entrance at street level with elevator to Orchestra and Dress Circle. No elevator to Balcony.
